title: Investigate planar-walk angular sort at seam-crossing nodes
description: PATCH-92 follow-up: 70/128 T-junctions on rocker-arm at alpha=15 land in dropped DCEL cycles, not in any emitted T-mesh patch. The 1844-half-arc giant cycle alone holds about half of these. PATCH-91 fixed corner DETECTION via TArc.directionAtStart/End (face-frame-correct cardinal classification at the node) but did NOT fix the angular SORT in TPatchEnumerator.outgoingByNode, which uses raw forwardStartAngle/reverseStartAngle computed in each arc's own start-face frame. At nodes where outgoing half-arcs come from different face frames (any seam crossing where motorcycles transition), this sort can mis-order them, sending the planar-dual face walk into a wrong neighbor. A single bad sort cascades into a giant DCEL cycle that swallows hundreds of T-junctions. Investigation: (a) audit TPatchEnumerator.outgoingByNode angular sort, (b) hypothesize: rotate angles into a common frame at each node using TRS rotations, (c) measure rocker-arm before/after via T-junction census (currently visible=12 hidden=46 lost=70 extended=3 of 128 expected).
definition-of-done: T-junction-lost-in-no-patch metric drops below 10%; giant DCEL cycle on rocker-arm shrinks below 100 half-arcs; planar walk produces a planar dual whose largest face has bounded corner count for genus-0 closed inputs.
testing-plan: 1) Add diagnostic that prints angular ordering at every seam-crossing node with at least 3 incident arcs. 2) Identify whether multi-face-frame outgoing arcs are sorted incorrectly. 3) Hypothesize fix: rotate every arc's angle into the node's home face frame via TRS lookup. 4) Compare T-junction census on rocker-arm before/after. Pass: 70-> below 13 lost T-junctions.
